trace.goal: Use a standout public-company quarter to discuss what it does and does not imply about the market.
expected_facts: The answer should treat Figma's quarter as impressive evidence, not proof that every SaaS company is healthy.
It should explain what makes the result notable at scale.
It should caution founders against overgeneralizing from one elite outlier.
rubric_must_haves: Uses the quarter to extract market or company-level lessons.
Explains why scale plus growth is notable.
Avoids turning one datapoint into a universal market conclusion.
trace.gold_reference: A strong answer should say that Figma's quarter is a reminder that elite SaaS companies can still post extraordinary numbers, especially when product expansion and AI tailwinds align. But founders should not confuse one exceptional company with a full market reset. The lesson is to separate the existence of winners from the claim that the whole sector has returned to easy mode.

Style examples from train-owned source text.

Do not copy long passages verbatim.
[Style 1]
A truly great human is still better than any AI agent at most complex, judgment-intensive work. Full stop. If you can find and keep exceptional people, do it. But here’s the honest truth: most hires aren’t great hires. A lot of folks don't want to discuss it, or want to challenge it. But deploying a great AI Agent is just easier, and less stressful, than making a mediocre hire. This is why 2027 will be brutal for tech employment. We'll default to picking an AI Agent over a human for many "hires" because it's just ... easier.
[Style 2]
I know so many CROs and VPs of Sales that used to be truly great ... And are just burnt now. Fried. Some tried to mask it by hiring CROs and VPs under them to do the work. And sometimes, that does work. But man sales isn't easy. Each month, each quarter, it's a new battle. It's epic but also can take its toll. Just make sure when you hire one with the perfect LinkedIn ... that they really, truly can go into battle again. Not just talk the talk. And share great stories, of epic battles past.

So Figma recently closed its first full quarter as a public company and man it was a good one:
Figma crossed $1B ARR
growing a stunning 41%
With $100m+ of net income
And 24% free cash flow margins
Just … wow.  Many of the public B2B and SaaS leaders may be struggling, in low growth mode.  But the best of it?  On fire.
5 Interesting Learnings:

#1. Enterprise Customers Continue to Accelerate at Scale
The Numbers
:
1,119 customers paying $100K+ ARR, up from 963 last quarter (+16% QoQ growth). This segment now represents the fastest-growing customer cohort.
Why This Matters
:
At $1B+ ARR run rate, growth increasingly comes from land-and-expand with large enterprises rather than new logo acquisition. The $100K+ cohort represents less than 10% of total paid customers but likely drives 40-60% of revenue.
Takeaway
:
Track your $100K+ ACV customers as a separate cohort early. At scale, this becomes your primary growth engine.
